'''Yuri S. Kivshar''' (born 3 April 1959) is a Ukrainian-born Australian physicist. He is a Distinguished Professor in the Research School of Physics at the [[Australian National University]] (ANU) in Canberra.<ref name="ANU-profile2">{{cite web |title=Yuri S. Kivshar |url=https://physics.anu.edu.au/contact/people/profile.php?ID=391 |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=Australian National University}}</ref> His research is in [[nonlinear optics]], [[Metamaterial|metamaterials]] and subwavelength photonics, ranging from [[Soliton|solitons]] to resonant [[Metasurface|metasurfaces]] and [[topological photonics]].<ref name="AP-interview2">{{cite journal |last1=Chang |first1=Guoqing |year=2021 |title=Journey from solitons to nanophotonics: an interview with Professor Yuri Kivshar |journal=Advanced Photonics |volume=3 |issue=1 |article-number=010502 |doi=10.1117/1.AP.3.1.010502|doi-access=free }}</ref> The [[Australian Academy of Science]] credits him with introducing the field of metaphotonics and names him as one of the founders of all-dielectric resonant metaphotonics.<ref name="AAS-20252">{{cite web |title=2025 awardees |url=https://science.org.au/our-work/awards-grants-programs/honorific-awardees/2025-awardees |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the Academy and a recipient of the 2022 [[Max Born Award]] of Optica and the Academy's 2025 [[Matthew Flinders Medal and Lecture|Matthew Flinders Medal]].

==Education==
Kivshar was born in Kharkiv, then part of the [[Soviet Union]] (now [[Ukraine]]).<ref name="AP-interview2" /> He received a master's degree in physics from the [[University of Kharkiv]] in 1981 and completed his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree (equivalent to a PhD) at the [[B Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering|Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering]] in 1984.<ref name="ANU-CV">{{cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae: Professor Yuri Kivshar |url=https://physics.anu.edu.au/contact/people/download_cv.php?PeopleID=391 |website=Australian National University, Research School of Physics |format=PDF |date=July 2018 |access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref>
==Career==
After early research on [[soliton]] dynamics in condensed matter and optics, Kivshar was an Alexander von Humboldt Research Fellow at the [[University of Düsseldorf]] from 1991 to 1993.<ref name="Optica-bio">{{cite web |title=Yuri S Kivshar |url=https://www.optica.org/history/biographies/bios/yuri_s_kivshar/ |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=Optica}}</ref> He joined the Australian National University in 1993, where he is a Distinguished Professor in the Research School of Physics.<ref name="ANU-profile2" /> In 2002 he founded the Nonlinear Physics Centre at ANU, which he heads,<ref name="ANU-2025">{{cite news |date=11 April 2025 |title=Academy honours nonlinear physicists |url=https://physics.anu.edu.au/news_events/?NewsID=385 |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=ANU Research School of Physics}}</ref> and from 2002 to 2017 he was Deputy Director of the ARC Centre for Ultrahigh-bandwidth Devices for Optical Systems (CUDOS).<ref name="CUDOS-2014">{{cite news |date=11 December 2014 |title=Professor Yuri Kivshar awarded prestigious Medal and Prize |url=http://www.cudos.org.au/news/2014-12-11_Kivshar_MasseyAward.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160229213111/http://www.cudos.org.au/news/2014-12-11_Kivshar_MasseyAward.shtml |archive-date=29 February 2016 |access-date=12 September 2026 |website=CUDOS, ARC Centre of Excellence for Ultrahigh-bandwidth Devices for Optical Systems}}</ref> In 2025 he was appointed Hung Hing Ying Distinguished Visiting Professor in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Hong Kong]].<ref name="HKU-staff">{{cite web |title=Academic Staff |url=https://www.physics.hku.hk/people/academic_staff/ |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=Department of Physics, The University of Hong Kong}}</ref> He is a deputy editor of ''Photonics Research'' and managing editor of the journal ''Nanophotonics'', and has served on the editorial boards of several optics and photonics journals.<ref name="Nanophotonics-ME">{{cite web |title=Nanophotonics |url=https://www.degruyter.com/view/j/nanoph |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801071020/https://www.degruyter.com/view/j/nanoph |archive-date=1 August 2019 |access-date=12 September 2026 |website=De Gruyter |quote=Managing Editors ... Yuri Kivshar, Australian National University, Australia}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Kivshar is a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] (elected 2002),<ref name="AAS-Fellow">{{cite web |title=Profile: Yuri Kivshar |url=https://science.org.au/about-us/academy-fellows/discover-our-fellows/yuri-kivshar |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref> Optica (2000), the [[American Physical Society]] (2006), the [[Institute of Physics]] and [[SPIE]]. He held Australian [[Federation Fellowship|Federation Fellowships]] from the [[Australian Research Council]] in 2002 and 2007.<ref name="ARC-2002">{{cite web |title=Federation Fellowships Funding outcome 2002 |url=http://www.arc.gov.au/ncgp/fedfellows/selection_discovery_fellow_02.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070829013433/http://www.arc.gov.au/ncgp/fedfellows/selection_discovery_fellow_02.htm |archive-date=29 August 2007 |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=Australian Research Council}}</ref>

* [[Matthew Flinders Medal and Lecture|Matthew Flinders Medal]], [[Australian Academy of Science]] (2025)<ref name="AAS-20252" />
* ZEISS Research Award (2025), shared with [[Jelena Vučković]]{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* [[Max Born Award]], [[Optica (society)|Optica]] (2022)<ref name="Optica-Fellow">{{cite web |title=2022 Max Born Award Winner |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/awards/2022_award_winner_pressreleases/2022bornmedalwinner/ |access-date=15 July 2026 |website=Optica}}</ref>
* Mozi Award, [[SPIE]] (2020){{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* [[Alexander von Humboldt Research Award]] (2017){{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* Harrie Massey Medal and Prize, [[Institute of Physics]] (2015){{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* Ukraine State Prize in Science and Technology (2013), for a body of work on nonlinear waves and solitons in condensed matter physics{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* [[Thomas Ranken Lyle Medal]], [[Australian Academy of Science]] (2007){{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* [[Walter Boas Medal]], [[Australian Institute of Physics]] (2005){{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
